summary.text: 问 means “ask” or “inquire” and is the standardized simplified form of 問. The received analysis of 問 assigns 口 a meaning role and 門 a sound role; the supplied comparisons do not independently establish their historical sound correspondence.

formation.text: The received analysis treats 問 as phonosemantic: 口 contributes meaning in association with speech, while 門 is assigned the phonetic role. The supplied historical reconstructions do not independently confirm the sound correspondence. In 问, 門 is written 门 as part of the standardized simplified form.

components.text: In 問, 口 is the semantic element in the received analysis, associating the character with speech. No distinct earlier form for this component is specified.

In 問, 門 is identified as the phonetic element. Modern and reconstructed readings can be compared, but the supplied evidence does not independently establish the proposed historical sound correspondence.

sound_limitation.text: The Baxter–Sagart readings are actual same-system readings for 門 and 問, but this comparison does not by itself verify the historical component analysis or sound relationship.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 門 is mén and 問 is wèn; this current comparison does not establish their historical relationship.
Baxter–Sagart 2014 gives 門 *mˤə[r] and 問 *C.mu[n]-s in its Old Chinese system. This comparison is relevant to the proposed phonetic analysis but does not independently establish it.

components.text: In 问, 门 is the standardized simplified form corresponding to traditional 門. This script-form relationship does not itself establish a historical sound role in 问.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin readings are reported as 门 mén and 问 wèn, but this current pair does not establish a historical phonetic relation in the simplified graph. The phonetic role described for traditional 問 belongs to the received analysis of that graph.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 门 is mén and 问 is wèn. This pair describes current readings only; it does not establish the historical sound relation.

history.text: The selected image is a modern vector redraw in Shuowen-style seal script. It illustrates the received dictionary form of 問, but is not an excavated artifact and does not establish a graphic sequence from the disputed Shang forms.

Two Shang graphs combining 門 and 口 were traditionally catalogued as 問. A later paleographic argument disputes that identification and their ancestry to the later 問 graph; it tentatively proposes they may instead be expanded forms of 啟, while leaving their inscriptional meaning unclear.

The earliest clear graph for the word “ask” or “inquire” in the surveyed evidence is reported in late Warring States Qin slips. Earlier graphs read as 聞 or 昏 were also used to write the spoken word 問. This is graphic reuse for a similar-sounding word, not a development of the meaning “hear” into “ask.”

A separate proposal derives the spoken word 問 from 聞 with an exoactive suffix, roughly “let me hear.” This proposed word history is distinct from the documented use of 聞 or 昏 graphs to write 問, and the supplied evidence does not independently verify it.

uncertainties.text: The identity and meaning of the Shang 門-and-口 graphs, and their relationship to 問, remain disputed. The proposal that they are expanded forms of 啟 is tentative.

The received analysis assigns 門 a phonetic role. Modern and Baxter–Sagart comparisons are available, but the evidence supplied does not independently establish the historical correspondence. The proposed derivation from 聞 plus a suffix is also unverified here.
The late Warring States Qin-slip examples and their precise chronology are reported in a scholarly discussion; the primary slip records have not been independently checked.

Current definitions include “ask about” and “inquire after.”

Modern Mandarin gives 门 mén and 问 wèn, but the supplied evidence does not independently establish the historical sound correspondence for the simplified graph.
